newsitem.title: LEBANON: SOLIDERE shares mixed on second day of BSE trade.
newsitem.headline: SOLIDERE shares mixed on second day of BSE trade.

text.p: SOLIDERE shares were mixed on Tuesday -- the second day of trade on the official Beirut Stock exchange (BSE).
B shares, issued in a $650 million flotation in January 1994, rose to $120 from $116. They stood at $113 on their last closing on the privately-operated Beirut Secondary Market (BSM) on Friday.
A shares, distributed to former holders of property rights in the Beirut central district which the company is rebuilding, dropped to $113 from $115.125 on Monday.
Turnover was 5,192 shares from Monday's 5,352 and the value of traded SOLIDERE shares was $606,009 from $610,759.
Also traded on the BSE were 3,000 Ciments Libanais shares at $1.3125, unchanged from September 20.
There was no trade in any of the three other listed companies: Ciments Blancs, Eternit and Uniceramic.

Dealers say the SOLIDERE switch is positive for the development of Lebanon's re-emerging capital markets. The move added some $2 billion to the capitalisation of the BSE, which had a total capitalisation of below $400 million.
The LISPI stock index rose 0.22 percent to 84.71 and BLOM stock index rose 0.04 percent to 989.52.
